the application of visual attributes for the visualisation of complex information.

the application of visual attributes to the effective display of complex information and we have found that the use of the classification of visual attributes can lead to the design of effective visualisations.
the application of perceptual concepts and principles to the design of effective and accurate visualisation techniques.

the visualisation schema is a powerful and flexible tool for the visualisation of complex data sets.

the visual attributes are a useful and important component of information visualisations, but that their application must be carefully considered and their use must be tailored to the specific information to be visualised.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new classification of perceptual attributes and that the results of our experiments show that the attributes can be used to effectively visualise complex information.
visualisation is a process of information transformation from the original information to the visual representation.
we have shown that it is possible to classify visual attributes in such a way that we can quantify their information density and information accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the information content of a visual attribute is not necessarily related to its spatial extent and that the classification of attributes can be used to design visualisations that are more effective for the visualisation of complex information.

visual attributes should be selected according to the type of data they are to represent, rather than the type of data that they are to convey, and that visual attributes with high information density are more appropriate for the visualisation of large datasets.
there is a tradeoff between the information content and spatial requirements for visual attributes.
